role: Director, Air Pollution Control Agency, New Hampshire Department of Health & Welfare
stance_basis: direct quote stating ORVs should be permitted under strict control with regulated areas
summary: Terrest H. Bunford, Director of the Air Pollution Control Agency at the New Hampshire Department of Health & Welfare, submitted an inter-department communication expressing a conditional stance on ORV use. He supports permitting ORVs under strict control, with areas of use regulated by the proper agency, and notes that any federal regulation should be consistent with existing state laws regarding safety features and licenses. He also observes that the federal government does not appear to be infringing on private landowners' rights.
complaint_summary: Bunford states that ORVs should be permitted under strict control with areas regulated by the proper agency, consistent with state laws on safety and licensing, and that federal regulation does not appear to infringe on private landowners' rights.

statement.text:
This proposed Executive Order as prepared by the Bureau of Outdoor Padredtion has given several aiternate proposals and various comments on quantions relative to the usage and control of ATV on Federal lends. .
Our personal opinion is that the vehicle should be permitted under strict control and the areas of use should be controlled and regulated by the proper agency, as they are to some extent by the state. Any regulation by the Federal people would be consistent with state laws and regulations relative to safety features and licenses, atc. There is no attempt by the Federal government, at least as we see it, to infringe upon the rights of private land owners at this time.
